source_caption:
Mark Wahlberg is almost unrecognizable as real-life Mafia hitman Gregory Scarpa in By Any Means.

For the role, Wahlberg underwent a major transformation, spending hours in the makeup chair with facial prosthetics, including an altered nose and chin, along with a wig, thick sideburns and 1960s-style costumes. The goal was to make him disappear into the role of Scarpa, one of New York’s most dangerous mobsters who secretly worked as an FBI informant.

And the story behind the movie is just as unbelievable.

Set in 1960s Mississippi, By Any Means follows a young FBI agent, Wayne Strider, played by Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, as the FBI struggles to solve the murder of civil rights leader Vernon Dahmer.

Dahmer had helped Black residents pay their poll taxes so they could register to vote. After his murder, investigators found that nobody in the community was willing to talk to the FBI. So they turned to Scarpa.

The real-life mobster was brought from New York to Mississippi and partnered with the FBI to help crack the case using methods that were far outside the bureau’s usual playbook.

It’s a bizarre true story about two completely different men working together for the same goal — and now it’s been turned into a crime thriller.

By Any Means is now available to watch digitally at home

source_details.synopsis: By Any Means is an American thriller directed by Leighton Spence and starring Brooke Burfitt, Thomas Gipson, Jonathan Cheban, and Michelle Money. The film had its first screening in Ireland before a run of international film festivals around the world in 2016. Gravitas Ventures acquired the distribution rights of the film, which was released by video on demand and on DVD on June 27, 2017.
